concept_name: AC Voltage Applied to a Capacitor
source_book: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Ch.7 Alternating Current, §7.4 AC Voltage Applied to a Capacitor — table-of-contents reference only; teaching authored from first principles, no sequence/example/figure imported. Third of 8 in the founder-reordered Ch.7 map (ac_voltage_resistor -> ac_voltage_inductor -> ac_voltage_capacitor -> phasors -> series_lcr_circuit -> ac_power_factor -> lc_oscillations -> transformer; phasors sits AFTER all three individual element concepts, so this diamond must stand entirely on time-domain reasoning -- no rotating-vector diagram appears anywhere). The atomic idea: a pure capacitor's current LEADS its applied sinusoidal voltage by EXACTLY a quarter cycle (90 degrees) because charge must flow onto the plates before the plate voltage can build (i = C dv/dt: the current is the voltage's SLOPE, not its size), so the current is geometrically forced to crest exactly where the voltage's slope is steepest; the opposition is a frequency-made reactance X_C = 1/(omega*C) which FALLS as frequency rises (the opposite of the inductor's reactance) and blocks DC outright; and the average power is EXACTLY zero -- every joule parked in the field between the plates during one quarter cycle is fully returned during the next. SCOPE: the inductor's mirror (lagging) behaviour (taught in ac_voltage_inductor, sealed), the rotating-vector/phasor formalism (deferred to phasors -- next), capacitor DC charging transients / RC time constants (already taught in the shipped capacitance concept, callback only), and combining C with R and L (deferred to series_lcr_circuit). Conceptual-only (no mode_overrides), EPIC-L-first (no epic_c_branches; the three misconceptions -- 'reactive components delay the current, so this must lag like the coil', 'opposition grows with frequency and size, the way it did for the coil', and 'the plates pushing back all cycle must cost energy like a resistor' -- are confronted inside EPIC-L via Rule 16a misconception_watch at exactly S2, S5, S7, each a straightforward contrast beat, no predict->reveal). Routed to the NEW field_3d 'ac_capacitor' scenario -- a parallel-plate apparatus (not a coil) with cool blue-cyan breathing inter-plate field lines, charge glyphs that pile INTO one plate and drain OUT of the other (never crossing the gap), a dual-strip scope pane (a clock-drawn i-trace LEADING plus a static dashed quarter-LATE 'ghost' hypothesis -- literally the inductor's own current trace -- plus an explicit time-order LEAD bracket with a drawn arrow), a SIGNED p-strip crossing zero, a tangent-walk cursor riding the V-TRACE (the cause) for the PRIMARY-aha state, a scripted closed-form f-ramp for the reactance state (response INVERTED from the inductor's: the current envelope SWELLS as frequency rises), a breathing U = half*C*v-squared stored-energy gauge peaking at the voltage's OWN crest, and a re-tasked avg_p meter held dead at 0.00 W -- built in-loop for this concept (docs/loop_runs/ch7_engine_log.md, commit 21e1f0f) as a CLEAN STANDALONE SIBLING of the sealed ac_resistor and ac_inductor scenarios (no acr_/acl_-prefixed code touched). entry_state_map's PRIMARY aha (S4, the current-copies-the-slope insight) sits INSIDE the foundational slice (S1-S4), so no mandatory exit-pill is required; optional cross-slice pills route foundational -> reactance (S5) -> power (S6-S7) -> derivation (S8). Every state is live (show_sliders true, Rule 31) but exposes only its own relevant control row(s): vm at S4 (plain live, no scripted driver), f_demo at S5 (scripted ramp + drag-seize + thumb-lockstep), ALL THREE (vm/f_demo/C) at S9 (explore). Frequency is deliberately LOCKED in S1-S4 -- dragging f here changes the current's amplitude and would pre-spoil S5's own reveal; capacitance C is LOCKED until S9 -- its own inversion (bigger C = less opposition) is a narration clause at S5, explored live only in the sandbox. Handoff from ac_voltage_inductor (prior concept): this diamond mirrors that exact arc (ghost-compare -> mechanism -> slope/lead -> reactance -> power slosh) for a cheap L<->C symmetry that series_lcr_circuit will exploit -- X_L = X_C = 5.00 ohms at the chapter's shared defaults is deliberate and unmentioned here (the S7 'same size, opposite clock' clause is the only permitted whisper); no fix cycle on this concept may ever add a phasor arrow.

real_world_anchor.primary: Inside the same two-way loudspeaker whose coil guards the bass driver, a capacitor sits in front of the tweeter. It is the coil's exact mirror: it lets the treble through and blocks the bass — the SAME capacitor, opposing different frequencies by different amounts, X_C = 1/(ωC) doing its job in the opposite direction. And like the coil, it does this without warming up: a resistor there would waste the music as heat; the capacitor merely borrows energy into the field between its plates and hands it back.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The smoothing capacitor inside every phone charger, placed across the output precisely because fast ripple slips through it easily while steady DC cannot pass at all — the 'blocks DC, welcomes fast AC' limit as a device every student owns. Mains frequency is phrased neutrally throughout — 'the mains frequency', never a fixed regional number.

f_demo.name: Demo-compressed AC frequency (real mains is tens of Hz)

theta.name: Instantaneous phase — native radians, state-local clock (Rule 26)
theta.derived: theta = omega * t   [EXCEPT S5 while undragged, which uses the closed-form ramp-phase accumulator of the S5 lemma in place of omega*t]

X_C.name: Capacitive reactance — the capacitor's frequency-made opposition (source-string token: literal ASCII X_C, capital C, underscore)

im.name: Peak (amplitude) current
im.derived: im = vm / X_C = omega * C * vm

v_C.name: Instantaneous plate voltage (ideal capacitor: identically equals v)
v_C.derived: v_C = v   [an ideal capacitor's own voltage always answers the source EXACTLY, at every instant — this identity is WHY i must equal C*dv/dt: v_C has no independent freedom to lag or smooth]

i.name: Instantaneous current
i.derived: i = im * sin(theta + PI/2) = im * cos(theta)   [LEADS v by exactly PI/2 rad = 90° = T/4, always]

slope_v.name: Instantaneous slope of v — the S4 PRIMARY-aha value, the tangent-walk cursor's live number
slope_v.derived: slope_v = vm * omega * cos(theta)   [= dv/dt exactly; i = C * slope_v identically, since C*vm*omega*cos(theta) = im*cos(theta) — NEVER a hardcoded 15.7, since vm is live-draggable at S4]

q_max.name: Maximum plate charge — the S5 constant-cargo readout, frequency-INDEPENDENT

p.name: Instantaneous power delivered TO the capacitor (S6/S8) — SIGNED, opposite sign convention from ac_voltage_inductor's p
p.derived: p = v * i = (vm*im/2) * sin(2*theta)   [+ = storing into the field, − = field returning energy to the source; STORE-quarter-first]

p_avg.name: Cycle-average power — EXACT zero, over an interval as short as T/2 = π/ω

U.name: Energy stored in the capacitor's E-field, instantaneous — the U-gauge value
U.derived: U = 0.5 * C * v^2 = Umax * sin(theta)^2   [breathes 0 <-> Umax TWICE per source period T, peaking at v's OWN crest — dU/dt = p(t) exactly]

Umax.name: Maximum stored energy — the U-gauge's ceiling AND the p-strip store-lobe's shaded area

lead_seconds.name: Time lead between the i-peak and the next v-peak — the S2 bracket's number

lead_degrees.name: Phase lead in degrees — frequency-INDEPENDENT, always exactly a quarter cycle

bead_frac.name: Micro-band wire-bead position fraction, 0/1=ends 0.5=home (Rule 33b)
bead_frac.derived: bead_frac = 0.5 + A_frac * sin(theta)   [beads are at MAXIMUM speed exactly at theta=0 (v=0, i=im, the S1 'full flood' plant) and MOMENTARILY AT REST exactly at theta=pi/2 (v-crest, i=0, the S1 'frozen' plant)]

A_frac.name: Bead-excursion visual scale, calibrated to 0.30 at defaults

charge_glyph_frac.name: Plate charge-glyph density fraction, 0=empty 1=full (Rule 33c)
charge_glyph_frac.derived: charge_glyph_frac = abs(sin(theta))   [= |q|/q_max; polarity/direction = sign(q) = sign(sin(theta)) — glyphs pile INTO one plate and drain OUT of the other, NEVER cross the gap]

field_brightness.name: Inter-plate E-field brightness/density — cool blue/geometric ONLY, the plates BODY never receives this or any emissive (Rule 33d)
field_brightness.derived: field_brightness = U/Umax = sin(theta)^2 = v^2/vm^2   [peaks EXACTLY at v's own crest — the 'field brightest while beads freeze' S1 plant; = 0 exactly at v=0 — the companion 'beads at full flood while the plates are empty' half of the same plant]

arrow_dir.name: Wire-current arrow direction / charge-glyph polarity sense
arrow_dir.derived: arrow_dir = sign(i) = sign(cos(theta))   [flips at i's own zero crossings — the v-crest/trough instants — a full quarter-cycle BEFORE v's own zero crossings. ONE flip schedule drives BOTH the wire arrow and the plate charge-glyph polarity here]

formulas.instantaneous_voltage: v = vₘ sin(ωt) — the applied AC voltage, ω = 2πf_demo
formulas.plate_voltage_tracks_source: v_C = v — an ideal capacitor's own voltage answers the source EXACTLY, at every instant (S3)
formulas.defining_relation: i = C·(dv/dt) — the defining law: current is the RATE charge must arrive, never v's size (S4 PRIMARY aha)
formulas.instantaneous_current: i = iₘ sin(ωt + 90°) = iₘ cos(ωt), iₘ = vₘ/X_C — current LEADS voltage by exactly a quarter cycle
formulas.reactance: X_C = 1/(ωC) — the frequency-made opposition; X_C FALLS as ω rises (opposite the coil) and X_C→∞ as ω→0 (a steady/DC capacitor draws no current — blocks DC outright)
formulas.plate_charge: q = Cv, q_max = Cvₘ — frequency-INDEPENDENT (S5's constant-cargo number)
formulas.instantaneous_power: p = v·i = +(vₘiₘ/2) sin(2ωt) — SIGNED, symmetric about zero, twice the source frequency; STORE-quarter-first (opposite sign from ac_voltage_inductor's p)
formulas.average_power: ⟨p⟩ = 0 EXACTLY — not approximately — over any interval that is a whole multiple of T/2 = π/ω
formulas.stored_energy: U = ½Cv² = Umax sin²(ωt), Umax = ½Cvₘ² — breathes 0↔Umax twice per source period, peaking at v's OWN crest; dU/dt = p(t) exactly
formulas.lobe_area_link: ∫ p dt over any store quarter = Umax exactly
formulas.point_symmetry_fold: p(t_c+τ) = −p(t_c−τ) at any zero crossing t_c of p(t) — every positive STORE lobe is the exact 180°-point-rotation of its trailing negative RETURN lobe about their shared zero crossing (S8's fold)
formulas.closed_form_derivation: q = Cv → i = C·dv/dt = ωCvₘ cos ωt = iₘ sin(ωt + π/2); the ω landing UPSTAIRS (multiplying) IS X_C's falling-with-frequency behaviour, and the +cos IS the 90° lead — one differentiation yields both headline results (S8)

constraints: i(t) = im sin(ωt + π/2) LEADS v(t) = vm sin(ωt) by EXACTLY π/2 rad (90°, T/4) at every instant — never lags, never in-phase, for a pure ideal capacitor.

v_C(t) = v(t) exactly, at every instant — an ideal capacitor's own voltage always equals the source's; i = C dv/dt is the SLOPE of that shared voltage, never v's value directly (the entire content of the PRIMARY aha).
X_C = 1/(ωC) FALLS as frequency rises and as capacitance rises; X_C → ∞ as ω → 0 (a steady/DC capacitor draws zero current once charged — blocks DC outright).
p(t) = v(t)·i(t) = +(vm·im/2)·sin(2ωt) is exactly odd-symmetric about every one of its own zero crossings — store and return lobe areas cancel PAIRWISE and exactly, never approximately, so ⟨p⟩ = 0.
U(t) = ½Cv(t)² ≥ 0 always; dU/dt = p(t) exactly — the U-gauge and the p-strip are the SAME physics, never independently scripted.
q_max = Cvm is frequency-INDEPENDENT — only the TIME available to deliver it (T/4 = 1/(4f)) shrinks as f rises, which is why im = ω·q_max grows with frequency even though q_max itself never changes.

aha_moment.statement: Current is the rate charge arrives — the lead is pure geometry, not capacitor magic.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The tangent cursor rides the voltage trace and steepens exactly at the zero crossings while the current dot answers at the same instant — the lead falls straight out of the slope relationship, not the capacitor's material.

STATE_1.title: Same source, new component: two parallel plates

scene_composition.text: same alternating source as before
charges flood in right when voltage is zero
field between the plates peaks at the voltage crest

tts_sentences.text_en: Same alternating source, but now it feeds parallel plates instead of a coil — everything still oscillates.
Watch the charges rush at full flood the instant the voltage reads zero.
And freeze completely at the voltage's peak, exactly where the field between the plates glows brightest.
Frequency's slowed down; mains runs tens of hertz.

STATE_2.title: The current leads the voltage by a quarter cycle

scene_composition.text: dashed guess: last lesson's quarter-late rhythm
real current sweeps in, arriving early
1.0 s = one quarter cycle = 90 degrees, ahead

tts_sentences.text_en: Here's the dashed guess: last lesson's coil current, arriving a quarter cycle late.
But this capacitor's charges refuse to obey — they surge at full flood, not backward.
Watch the real current sweep in — same size, but arriving early instead.
It crests a full quarter cycle before the voltage — ninety degrees ahead.

misconception_watch.belief: Reactive components delay the current — a capacitor's current will lag like the coil's did.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The dashed quarter-late ghost trace docks first, the beads visibly disobey it by surging forward at full flood, and the real current crests a full quarter cycle EARLY with the lead bracket confirming one quarter cycle equals ninety degrees.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The coil holds current back; the capacitor demands it up front — a quarter cycle early, not late.

STATE_3.title: The plates fill and push back against the source

scene_composition.text: voltage climbs: charge piles onto the plates
source eases: plates pour that charge back
plate voltage always tracks the source, volt for volt

tts_sentences.text_en: Zoom into the plates: as voltage climbs, charge pours in, current dies away.
At the crest the plates are full — current is zero, right where the field burns brightest.
The source eases, charge pours back out — current reverses before the voltage does; charge never crosses this ideal, resistance-free, demo-scale capacitor's gap.

STATE_4.title: Current copies the slope — the PRIMARY aha

scene_composition.text: current follows voltage's slope, not its size
voltage steepest: current at its own peak
voltage flat at the crest: current is zero

tts_sentences.text_en: The rule: current follows voltage's slope, not its size.
Where voltage crosses zero, climbing steepest, current sits at its peak.
Where voltage peaks and flattens, current is exactly zero — the plates are full.
Falling steepest now — current dives to its trough. Drag peak voltage: tangents steepen, the lead never moves.

scene_composition.text: opposition equals one over angular frequency times capacitance
faster swing: current swells
slower swing: current starves

tts_sentences.text_en: This opposition isn't fixed like a resistor's — frequency makes it, and it runs backward.
Watch the swing speed up — the current swells, slipping through easily each cycle.
Slow it down and the current starves — steady voltage gets blocked completely.
The trick lets a speaker capacitor pass the treble, blocking the bass.

misconception_watch.belief: Opposition grows with frequency and with component size — the way it did for the coil.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The same capacitor, nothing about it changed, and as frequency ramps up the reactance readout FALLS from 5.0 to 2.5 ohms while the peak current SWELLS to 4.0 amps; winding frequency down starves the current instead, and a steady voltage is blocked entirely.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: X_C = 1/(ωC) — everything is downstairs: faster swings and bigger capacitors both mean LESS opposition; steady DC is blocked outright.

scene_composition.text: power equals voltage times current, every instant
same sign: storing — opposite sign: returning
shaded area equals the gauge's peak: 6.37 J

tts_sentences.text_en: Multiply voltage by current — power swings both positive and negative.
When they share a sign, power is positive — the field fills, storing energy.
When the signs disagree, power turns negative — the field drains, paying energy back.
That shaded area equals exactly what the gauge just filled — nothing is lost.

STATE_7.title: Nothing is consumed — average power is exactly zero

scene_composition.text: average-power meter: dead at zero
current still flows, field still breathes
plates: never warm

tts_sentences.text_en: Here's an averaging wattmeter — watch it stay dead at zero, cycle after cycle.
Peak current is clearly flowing, the field keeps breathing, and the gauge keeps filling and draining.
But the plates never warm — they borrow energy and hand it back; only resistance actually eats.

misconception_watch.belief: The plates push back all cycle, so charging must cost energy — a capacitor heats like a resistor.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The wattmeter needle stays dead at 0.00 watts while 2.00 amps of peak current visibly flows and the plates stay cold forever, unlike the resistor's steady 10.0 watt heater through the same size of opposition.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The plates store and return; only resistance eats.

scene_composition.text: one differentiation of charge equals capacitance times voltage
out falls both the 90-degree lead and the falling opposition
each power lobe rotates onto the next — average exactly zero

tts_sentences.text_en: Nothing moves here — just one differentiation: current equals capacitance times voltage's rate of change.
Out falls a positive cosine — the quarter-cycle lead — with angular frequency landing upstairs, shrinking the opposition.
The power curve folds exactly: each lobe rotates a half turn onto the next, canceling pair by pair.

STATE_9.title: Explore — the whole capacitor circuit, live

scene_composition.text: drag peak voltage, frequency, capacitance
watch the lead, the field, the current respond live
current leads voltage by one quarter cycle (90 degrees)

tts_sentences.text_en: It's all yours now — drag peak voltage, frequency, and capacitance, and watch the lead, the field, and the current respond live.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student has mastered AC voltage on a capacitor when they can (1) state that a pure capacitor's current leads its applied sinusoidal voltage by exactly a quarter cycle (90 degrees), never lags and is never in phase; (2) explain WHY the lead exists — charge must accumulate on the plates before the plate voltage can build, so the current (the rate charge is delivered) is largest exactly where the voltage is changing fastest, not where it is largest; (3) read off the current's instantaneous behaviour at any point in the voltage cycle — zero where voltage peaks (plates full), at its own peak where voltage crosses zero (steepest climb); (4) compute the peak current from the reactance, im = vm/X_C with X_C = 1/(omega*C), and predict how doubling the frequency (or the capacitance) changes it — the opposite trend from an inductor; (5) state that the cycle-average power delivered to a pure capacitor is exactly zero, and explain where the energy goes — stored in the electric field, then fully returned; (6) contrast reactance with resistance — a capacitor opposes current without ever dissipating energy, unlike a resistor; and (7) derive, from i = C dv/dt, both the 90-degree lead and the reactance X_C = 1/(omega*C) in one differentiation, and show that the resulting power p = v*i averages to exactly zero.

questions.stem: A pure capacitor (ideal, no resistance) carries a sinusoidal AC voltage. Compared to the voltage, how does the current behave?

options.A: The current peaks exactly a quarter cycle (90°) BEFORE the voltage — it leads
options.B: The current peaks exactly a quarter cycle (90°) AFTER the voltage — it lags
options.C: The current peaks at exactly the same instant as the voltage — zero phase difference
options.D: The current and voltage have no fixed timing relationship — it depends on the capacitance value

distractor_misconceptions.B: imports the inductor's lag behaviour (the sibling concept just taught) onto a capacitor
distractor_misconceptions.C: imports the resistor's in-phase rhythm — a different prior belief entirely
distractor_misconceptions.D: misses that an ideal capacitor's phase relationship is fixed at exactly 90° regardless of the capacitance value — only the reactance's SIZE depends on C, never the phase angle

questions.tested_idea: For a pure capacitor, current leads voltage by exactly a quarter cycle (90°) — never lags, never in phase.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A student says a capacitor's current 'copies the voltage but a bit early.' State the exact phase relationship, in degrees, and name which quantity is ahead.

questions.stem: WHY does a capacitor's current lead its voltage by exactly a quarter cycle?

options.A: Charge must physically accumulate on the plates before the plate voltage can build, so the current — the rate charge arrives — is largest right when the voltage is changing fastest, not when it is largest
options.B: The plates physically speed the electrons up as they approach the gap
options.C: The capacitor stores energy like an inductor and releases it later
options.D: The lead is just how AC works, no different from a plain wire

distractor_misconceptions.B: invents a mechanical electron-speeding mechanism with no physical basis
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses a capacitor's electric-field energy storage with an inductor's magnetic-field storage — different mechanism, different physics
distractor_misconceptions.D: denies the capacitor-specific mechanism entirely, missing that a plain wire (no real capacitance) shows no lead at all

questions.tested_idea: The lead exists because current is the RATE charge is delivered — i = C dv/dt, not because of the size of v.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Explain in one sentence why a capacitor's current can't simply track the size of the applied voltage the way a resistor's does.

questions.stem: At the exact instant a pure capacitor's voltage is at its POSITIVE PEAK, what is happening to the current?

options.A: The current is exactly zero — the plates are momentarily full and nothing more can arrive
options.B: The current is also at its positive peak
options.C: The current is at its negative peak
options.D: The current cannot be determined without knowing the capacitance

distractor_misconceptions.B: imports the resistor's in-phase behaviour onto a capacitor
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses 'voltage at peak' with 'current at peak' — the two peaks are a quarter cycle apart, not opposite
distractor_misconceptions.D: misses that the current's VALUE at this instant is zero regardless of capacitance — only iₘ's SIZE depends on C, never this timing fact

questions.tested_idea: Current is the SLOPE of voltage: at voltage's peak (flat slope) current is zero; at voltage's zero crossing (steepest slope) current is at its own peak.
questions.parallel_form_stem: At the instant a pure capacitor's voltage crosses zero, what is true of the current at that same instant?

questions.stem: A pure capacitor's peak current is im = omega*C*vm. If the frequency of the applied AC is doubled (voltage amplitude and capacitance unchanged), what happens to the peak current?

options.A: It doubles — the reactance halves, so the same peak voltage drives twice the peak current
options.B: It halves — a faster swing should choke more current, like it does for a coil
options.C: It stays the same — frequency doesn't affect a capacitor
options.D: It quadruples — reactance depends on frequency squared

distractor_misconceptions.B: imports the inductor's frequency response — the OPPOSITE trend — onto a capacitor
distractor_misconceptions.C: the confronted misconception — believes a component's opposition is fixed regardless of frequency
distractor_misconceptions.D: misremembers the reactance formula as frequency-squared rather than the linear (inverse) dependence the derivation actually produces

questions.tested_idea: Capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(ωC) FALLS as frequency rises, so peak current im = vm/X_C grows as frequency rises — the opposite trend from an inductor.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A capacitor passes 1.0 A peak at 0.1 Hz. Using the same capacitor and voltage, estimate the peak current at 0.5 Hz, and explain the trend.

questions.stem: A pure capacitor carries AC continuously. What is its average power consumption over a full cycle, and where does the energy delivered during part of the cycle go?

options.A: Average power is exactly zero — every joule stored in the electric field while the plates fill is returned to the source while they empty
options.B: Average power is exactly zero because no current is actually flowing
options.C: Average power is positive but small, since the capacitor has some leakage
options.D: Average power equals the peak instantaneous power, since current is always flowing somewhere in the circuit

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses 'zero average power' with 'zero current' — current visibly flows up to its peak the whole time
distractor_misconceptions.C: imports resistive leakage onto an IDEAL capacitor, which by definition has none
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses average power with peak power — very different numbers

questions.tested_idea: A pure capacitor's average power is EXACTLY zero — energy is stored in the field and fully returned, never dissipated.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A wattmeter reads a steady 0.00 W on a capacitor while an ammeter shows 2.00 A of current flowing. Explain how both readings can be true at once.

questions.stem: Starting from i = C(dv/dt) for a pure capacitor with v = vm*sin(omega*t), which pair of results falls out of ONE differentiation?

options.A: i = im*sin(omega*t + pi/2), where im = omega*C*vm — the 90° lead AND the reactance's inverse-frequency dependence both appear in the same expression
options.B: i = im*sin(omega*t), with no phase shift at all
options.C: i = im*cos(omega*t), with the reactance appearing as omega*C squared in the numerator
options.D: i = im*sin(omega*t − pi/2), lagging the voltage by 90°

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the phase shift entirely — imports the resistor's in-phase result
distractor_misconceptions.C: misremembers the reactance dependence produced by the differentiation
distractor_misconceptions.D: gets the SIGN of the phase shift backwards — a lead, not a lag (that's the inductor's earlier result)

questions.tested_idea: One differentiation of q = Cv yields both the 90° lead (the +cos term) and the reactance's ω-dependence (ω landing upstairs, multiplying) together.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Starting from i = C dv/dt, derive the expression for instantaneous power p(t) and show that its cycle-average is exactly zero.
